papers.title: Seumetry: a versatile and comprehensive R toolkit to accelerate high-dimensional flow and mass cytometry data analysis
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Recent progress in flow and mass cytometry technologies enables the simultaneous measurement of over 50 parameters for an individual cell. The resulting increase in data volume and complexity present challenges for conventional analysis methods, which are based on manual gating, are time-consuming and fail to capture unknown or minor cell populations. Advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) technologies have prompted the development of computational analysis tools designed to process and analyze high-dimensional biological data. Building on these advances, we here present Seumetry, a framework that combines flow and mass cytometry data-specific analysis methods with the capabilities of Seurat, a powerful tool for the analysis of scRNAseq data. Results Seumetry offers methods for advanced quality control, data visualizations, and differential population abundance and protein expression analysis. We tested Seumetry on an in-house generated complex dataset of immune cells from different layers of human intestines, demonstrating that Seumetry accurately identifies distinct immune cell populations. Furthermore, benchmarking against public datasets showed that Seumetry aligns with manual-gated results, further validating its use for high-dimensional flow and mass cytometry data. In summary, Seumetry provides a new scalable framework for the comprehensive analysis of high-dimensional cytometry data with seamless integration into commonly used scRNAseq analysis tools, enabling in-depth analysis methods to facilitate biological interpretations. Availability Seumetry code is available open source under an MIT license and the current version can be viewed and used via Github: https://github.com/imsb-uke/Seumetry ; and archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21216681 . Flow cytometry data generated for this manuscript is available via Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11935872

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
近年来，流式细胞术与质谱细胞术技术的进步使得人们能够同时检测单个细胞的50多种生物学参数。然而，由此产生的海量数据及其复杂性给基于手动分选的常规分析方法带来了挑战——这些方法耗时且无法有效识别那些未知或数量较少的细胞群体。单细胞RNA测序技术的突破进一步推动了用于处理高维生物数据的计算分析工具的发展。在此基础上，我们开发了Seumetry这一框架，它将流式细胞术与质谱细胞术的数据分析方法与Seurat这一强大的单细胞RNA测序数据分析工具相结合，从而实现了高效的数据处理与分析。  

**结果**  
Seumetry提供了先进的质量控制机制、数据可视化工具以及用于检测不同细胞群体丰度及蛋白质表达的分析方法。我们使用来自人类肠道不同组织的免疫细胞数据对Seumetry进行了测试，结果表明该框架能够准确识别各种免疫细胞类型。此外，通过与公开数据集的对比验证，我们进一步证明了Seumetry在处理高维流式/质谱细胞数据方面的有效性。  

**总结**  
Seumetry为高维细胞生物学数据的综合分析提供了可扩展的解决方案，并能与常用的单细胞RNA测序分析工具无缝集成，从而帮助研究人员深入挖掘数据背后的生物学意义。该框架的源代码基于MIT许可证公开发布，当前版本可通过GitHub获取：https://github.com/imsb-uke/Seumetry；相关数据也存储在Zenodo平台上：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21216681。本研究中使用的流式细胞术数据同样可在Zenodo上查阅：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11935872。

papers.title: Letters and Biological Process: Linguistic Structure Encodes Hierarchical Depth in the Gene Ontology
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation We asked whether the natural language used to name Gene Ontology (GO) Biological Process terms encodes hierarchical position in the GO directed acyclic graph. Results Semantic representations of term names, combined with UMAP visualization and k-means clustering (k=20) recovered biologically coherent semantic groups whose depth distributions differed strongly (Kruskal–Wallis H=5244, p<10−300; η2=0.217). Term-name length increased with depth (Pearson r=0.34, Spearman ρ=0.37; slope ≈3.2 letters per level), and this positive scaling held under shortest-, longest-, and average-path depth definitions. Vocabulary entropy followed a bell-shaped diversification–specialization curve with an intermediate-depth peak (maximal at depth 4) that lies outside a Monte Carlo null envelope across most depths, and null-model tests supported a genuine linguistic–hierarchical association. papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
我们探讨了用于命名基因本体论（GO）生物过程术语的自然语言是否能够反映这些术语在GO有向无环图中的层次结构。  

**研究结果**  
通过结合术语名称的语义表征、UMAP可视化技术以及k均值聚类分析（k=20），我们发现了具有生物学意义的词汇群组，这些群组的深度分布存在显著差异（Kruskal–Wallis检验H值=5244，p<10^−300；η²=0.217）。研究发现，术语名称的长度与其所代表的层次深度呈正相关关系（Pearson相关系数r=0.34，Spearman相关系数ρ=0.37；每增加一个层次，术语长度约增加3.2个字母），这一规律在采用不同路径长度定义的情况下依然成立。词汇的熵值变化遵循钟形曲线，其中在中等深度处出现峰值（最大值为第4层），且在大多数深度范围内，这一分布都不符合随机模型的预期结果；零模型检验进一步证实了语言结构与层次关系之间的真实关联性。  

**资源获取**  
go_lingdepth Python包、重新生成的结果表格以及图表生成脚本均可在以下链接获取：https://github.com/Sadiya-ISU/Letters-and-Biological-Process，同时这些资源也存储在Zenodo平台上。

papers.title: Inverse probability weighting-based mediation analysis for microbiome data
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Mediation analysis is an important tool for elucidating causal mechanisms in biomedical research and has recently gained increasing attention in microbiome studies. Motivated by a microbiome study of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, we investigate whether the effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection status is mediated through gut microbial taxa. This problem poses substantial methodological challenges due to the high dimensionality, zero inflation, and dependence of microbial mediators, as well as the presence of an exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounder, antibiotic use. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel nonparametric identification formula for the interventional indirect effect, a causal mediation estimand that remains identifiable in the presence of exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounding. Building on this identification result, we develop an inverse probability weighting estimator and construct standard normal bootstrap confidence intervals for inference. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate effect estimation and maintains appropriate type I error rates and power in finite samples. Application to the AML microbiome study provides evidence of a statistically significant interventional indirect effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection risk through alterations in the gut microbiome. Availability and implementation The R code for the simulation studies is available at https://github.com/YX-ZHANG-1/CausalMediationMicrobiome and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21960802

papers.title: Efficient and scalable Python implementation of ANCOM-BC and ANCOM-BC2 for omics differential abundance testing
papers.summary: Abstract Summary Analysis of Compositions of Microbiomes with Bias Correction (ANCOM-BC) and its successor ANCOM-BC2 are critical algorithms for differential abundance analysis. Designed for handling compositional data, they feature the ability to estimate the unknown sampling fractions and correct the bias induced by their differences. While the original R package implementing the two methods is robust for standard dataset sizes, the increasing magnitude of modern multi-omics studies presents computational challenges, often resulting in a runtime bottleneck for high-dimensional data. Here, we present native Python implementations of both ANCOM-BC and ANCOM-BC2 in the scikit-bio package, significantly accelerating the workflow and enabling their application to large-scale datasets. By leveraging vectorization with NumPy and numerical optimization in SciPy, we enhanced the efficiency of both methods without compromising their statistical accuracy. The benchmarking results revealed a dramatic increase in performance in both simulated and real datasets. We demonstrated that our Python implementations generated test results matching the original R code, while achieving 380- and 147-fold faster runtimes and 97.4% and 96.2% lower memory consumption on the largest tested dataset, respectively. The Python implementations allow for the analysis of datasets that are significantly larger than previously possible, and enable applications to alternative omics data types and complex statistical models that vary greatly by the number of samples, features, and covariates. Availability and Implementation https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio

all_papers.title: Seumetry: a versatile and comprehensive R toolkit to accelerate high-dimensional flow and mass cytometry data analysis
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Recent progress in flow and mass cytometry technologies enables the simultaneous measurement of over 50 parameters for an individual cell. The resulting increase in data volume and complexity present challenges for conventional analysis methods, which are based on manual gating, are time-consuming and fail to capture unknown or minor cell populations. Advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) technologies have prompted the development of computational analysis tools designed to process and analyze high-dimensional biological data. Building on these advances, we here present Seumetry, a framework that combines flow and mass cytometry data-specific analysis methods with the capabilities of Seurat, a powerful tool for the analysis of scRNAseq data. Results Seumetry offers methods for advanced quality control, data visualizations, and differential population abundance and protein expression analysis. all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation We asked whether the natural language used to name Gene Ontology (GO) Biological Process terms encodes hierarchical position in the GO directed acyclic graph. Results Semantic representations of term names, combined with UMAP visualization and k-means clustering (k=20) recovered biologically coherent semantic groups whose depth distributions differed strongly (Kruskal–Wallis H=5244, p<10−300; η2=0.217). Vocabulary entropy followed a bell-shaped diversification–specialization curve with an intermediate-depth peak (maximal at depth 4) that lies outside a Monte Carlo null envelope across most depths, and null-model tests supported a genuine linguistic–hierarchical association. all_papers.title: Inverse probability weighting-based mediation analysis for microbiome data
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Mediation analysis is an important tool for elucidating causal mechanisms in biomedical research and has recently gained increasing attention in microbiome studies. Motivated by a microbiome study of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, we investigate whether the effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection status is mediated through gut microbial taxa. This problem poses substantial methodological challenges due to the high dimensionality, zero inflation, and dependence of microbial mediators, as well as the presence of an exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounder, antibiotic use. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel nonparametric identification formula for the interventional indirect effect, a causal mediation estimand that remains identifiable in the presence of exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounding. Building on this identification result, we develop an inverse probability weighting estimator and construct standard normal bootstrap confidence intervals for inference. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate effect estimation and maintains appropriate type I error rates and power in finite samples. Application to the AML microbiome study provides evidence of a statistically significant interventional indirect effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection risk through alterations in the gut microbiome. Availability and implementation The R code for the simulation studies is available at https://github.com/YX-ZHANG-1/CausalMediationMicrobiome and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21960802

**摘要**  
中介分析是阐明生物医学研究中因果机制的重要工具，在微生物组研究领域也受到了越来越多的关注。受一项针对急性髓系白血病患者进行的微生物组研究的启发，我们探讨了诱导化疗强度对感染状况的影响是否通过肠道微生物群这一中介因素来发挥作用的。由于该问题涉及高维度数据、零膨胀现象、微生物中介因子的依赖性，以及暴露因素与结局变量之间的混杂效应（如抗生素的使用），因此在方法学上存在诸多挑战。  

为应对这些挑战，我们提出了一种新的非参数识别公式，用于确定在存在暴露因素-结局变量混杂的情况下仍可识别的因果中介效应。基于这一识别结果，我们进一步开发了逆概率加权估计方法，并构建了标准正态自助法置信区间以进行统计推断。模拟实验表明，所提出的方法能够在有限样本条件下实现准确的效应估计，同时保持适当的I型错误率和检验功效。将这一方法应用于急性髓系白血病的微生物组研究后，我们发现了诱导化疗强度通过改变肠道微生物群结构，从而对感染风险产生显著影响的证据。  

**代码与数据资源**  
用于模拟研究的R代码可访问以下链接：https://github.com/YX-ZHANG-1/CausalMediationMicrobiome，并已存档于Zenodo平台：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21960802。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Mediation analysis is an important tool for elucidating causal mechanisms in biomedical research and has recently gained increasing attention in microbiome studies. Motivated by a microbiome study of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, we investigate whether the effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection status is mediated through gut microbial taxa. This problem poses substantial methodological challenges due to the high dimensionality, zero inflation, and dependence of microbial mediators, as well as the presence of an exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounder, antibiotic use. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel nonparametric identification formula for the interventional indirect effect, a causal mediation estimand that remains identifiable in the presence of exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounding. Building on this identification result, we develop an inverse probability weighting estimator and construct standard normal bootstrap confidence intervals for inference. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate effect estimation and maintains appropriate type I error rates and power in finite samples. Application to the AML microbiome study provides evidence of a statistically significant interventional indirect effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection risk through alterations in the gut microbiome.

all_papers.title: Efficient and scalable Python implementation of ANCOM-BC and ANCOM-BC2 for omics differential abundance testing
all_papers.summary: Abstract Summary Analysis of Compositions of Microbiomes with Bias Correction (ANCOM-BC) and its successor ANCOM-BC2 are critical algorithms for differential abundance analysis. Designed for handling compositional data, they feature the ability to estimate the unknown sampling fractions and correct the bias induced by their differences. While the original R package implementing the two methods is robust for standard dataset sizes, the increasing magnitude of modern multi-omics studies presents computational challenges, often resulting in a runtime bottleneck for high-dimensional data. Here, we present native Python implementations of both ANCOM-BC and ANCOM-BC2 in the scikit-bio package, significantly accelerating the workflow and enabling their application to large-scale datasets. By leveraging vectorization with NumPy and numerical optimization in SciPy, we enhanced the efficiency of both methods without compromising their statistical accuracy. The benchmarking results revealed a dramatic increase in performance in both simulated and real datasets. We demonstrated that our Python implementations generated test results matching the original R code, while achieving 380- and 147-fold faster runtimes and 97.4% and 96.2% lower memory consumption on the largest tested dataset, respectively. The Python implementations allow for the analysis of datasets that are significantly larger than previously possible, and enable applications to alternative omics data types and complex statistical models that vary greatly by the number of samples, features, and covariates. Availability and Implementation https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 摘要：带有偏差校正功能的微生物组组成分析算法ANCOM-BC及其后续版本ANCOM-BC2，是进行差异丰度分析的重要工具。这些算法专为处理组合数据而设计，能够估算未知的样本比例，并纠正因数据差异带来的偏差。虽然最初用于实现这两种方法的R语言包在处理标准规模的数据集时表现良好，但现代多组学研究规模的不断扩大给计算带来了巨大挑战，尤其是对于高维数据而言，运行速度常常成为瓶颈。为此，我们在scikit-bio包中提供了ANCOM-BC和ANCOM-BC2的Python实现版本，这些实现显著提升了算法的执行效率，使其能够应用于大规模数据集。通过利用NumPy的向量化技术及SciPy的数值优化功能，我们在不牺牲统计准确性的前提下大幅提高了算法性能。测试结果显示，在模拟数据集与真实数据集中，这两种Python实现的运行速度分别比原始R代码快了380倍和147倍，内存消耗也降低了97.4%和96.2%。这些Python实现使得分析规模远大于以往可能的范围，并且能够适用于各种类型的组学数据以及样本数量、特征变量数量差异较大的复杂统计模型。更多相关信息可访问：https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio
